expectations.text: The debrief does not attribute any registration count to the partnership and produces no estimated figure for the unattributed channels.
expectations.evidence: 'The partnership drove an unknown number'; the 70-140 is labeled 'arithmetic on an unsourced premise, not a finding.'

expectations.text: The claimed 5-10% industry figure is rejected, on the grounds that no industry-wide measured referral value for event-to-event swaps has been published.
expectations.evidence: 'I found no published measurement of how many registrations event-to-event swaps drive.'

expectations.text: Deliverables with no attributable result are recorded explicitly as unmeasured, never as estimated numbers.
expectations.evidence: The ledger's 'Attributed result' column reads 'Unmeasured' for every row.

expectations.text: The debrief includes a per-partner delivery ledger covering both directions, with dates and evidence links for each deliverable.
expectations.evidence: Table has Direction and 'Shipped / evidence' columns with Date/Link blanks, covering Them → us and Us → them.

expectations.text: The debrief asks the two relationship questions: was the collaboration easy, and do both sides want to recur.
expectations.evidence: 'Was it easy to work with them?' and 'Do both sides want to recur?'

expectations.text: The debrief ends with a recur, renegotiate, or drop decision that is communicated to the partner.
expectations.evidence: It recommends 'recur', but the only partner step is an open item: 'Decide whether to send GreenStack the recur proposal.' Communication of the decision is not committed.

expectations.text: The response prescribes attribution before launch for the next edition: per-partner codes, campaign-tagged links, or a registration source field.
expectations.evidence: 'Before the next edition launches: ...dedicated GreenStack code... Tagged links... source field'.

expectations.text: The debrief does not attribute any registration count to the partnership and produces no estimated figure for the unattributed channels.
expectations.evidence: States 'the partnership accounts for about 70 to 140 registrations' and suggests a midpoint of about 100 (roughly 7%) as a planning figure.

expectations.text: The claimed 5-10% industry figure is rejected, on the grounds that no industry-wide measured referral value for event-to-event swaps has been published.
expectations.evidence: It uses the 5-10% figure as a planning assumption. It only says 'I can't verify where the 5-10% figure comes from' and 'The benchmark is generic', and never rejects it.

expectations.text: Deliverables with no attributable result are recorded explicitly as unmeasured, never as estimated numbers.
expectations.evidence: It says 'We can't measure how many of our 1,400 registrations the partnership drove' and 'Tracking: None', but it also gives estimated numbers (70-140, midpoint about 100).

expectations.text: The debrief includes a per-partner delivery ledger covering both directions, with dates and evidence links for each deliverable.
expectations.evidence: Section 2 has a table of what each side gave, but it has no dates and no evidence links. Several cells say 'Not recorded'.

expectations.text: The debrief asks the two relationship questions: was the collaboration easy, and do both sides want to recur.
expectations.evidence: It asks only 'Do we renew with GreenStack? I'd say yes, but only with tracking in place.' It never asks whether the collaboration was easy or whether both sides want to recur.

expectations.text: The debrief ends with a recur, renegotiate, or drop decision that is communicated to the partner.
expectations.evidence: Section 7 poses renewal as a question for the committee, with no decision made and nothing said about telling GreenStack.

expectations.text: The response prescribes attribution before launch for the next edition: per-partner codes, campaign-tagged links, or a registration source field.
expectations.evidence: Recommendations: 'Give the partner a unique code and tracking link... UTM-tagged URL per partner' and 'Add "How did you hear about us?" to registration.'
